knowledge_point.title: Solving for a Vector in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}$ given that $3a-5x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ -8 \\ -4\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}30 \\ 4 \\ -44 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3a-5x & =b \\ -5x & =b-3a \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}(b-3a) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}(\begin{bmatrix}30 \\ 4 \\ -44 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ -8 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}30 \\ 10 \\ -20 \\ 10\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -2 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=-6+4=-2.$

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{2}-{x}_{4}$ given that  $6a-2x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -4 \\ 12 \\ 16\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -12 \\ -24 \\ -20\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6a-2x & =b \\ -2x & =b-6a \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}(b-6a) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}(\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -12 \\ -24 \\ -20\end{bmatrix}-6\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -4 \\ 12 \\ 16\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}-32 \\ 12 \\ -96 \\ -116\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -6 \\ 48 \\ 58\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{2}-{x}_{4}=-6-58=-64.$

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{3}-{x}_{2}$ given that  $4a+3x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}18 \\ -15 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4a+3x & =b \\ 3x & =b-4a \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}(b-4a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}(\begin{bmatrix}18 \\ -15 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}-4\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ -27 \\ -21\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -9 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{3}-{x}_{2}=-7-(-9)=2.$

question.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{4}-{x}_{1}$ given that  $6a-2x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ -6 \\ 18 \\ 24\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ -18 \\ -36 \\ -30\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6a-2x & =b \\ -2x & =b-6a \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}(b-6a) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}(\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ -18 \\ -36 \\ -30\end{bmatrix}-6\begin{bmatrix}12 \\ -6 \\ 18 \\ 24\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}-48 \\ 18 \\ -144 \\ -174\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}24 \\ -9 \\ 72 \\ 87\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{4}-{x}_{1}=87-24=63.$
